# Basics: status, doctor, version, help, login, logout

The commands that are a whole domain. `orca status` first when anything looks wrong.

## `orca status [--disk]`

one screen: is the panel answering, what work waits on a person, and the facts around it (read-only, starts nothing)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.
- `--disk`: also report disk use: the run/workspace roots, artifacts and staging, and the five largest run directories
- Exit codes: 0 every check ok (warnings allowed); 1 a check failed.

```
orca status
orca status --json
orca status --disk
```

## `orca gc [--apply] [--older-than <older-than>] [--keep-last <keep-last>] [--include-uncleaned] [--group <group>]`

reclaim disk from settled runs in archived groups: <stateDir>.runs/<runId> and <stateDir>.workspaces/<runId> only; dry run by default

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.
- `--apply`: actually delete (default: print what would be removed and how much it would free)
- `--older-than <n>`: keep runs touched within this many days (default 30)
- `--keep-last <n>`: keep the newest N runs regardless of age
- `--include-uncleaned`: also reclaim runs whose driver never finished its cleanup (marked in the plan; every other guard still holds)
- `--group <group>`: limit to one group's runs
- Exit codes: 0 the plan ran (dry run, or applied); 1 refused here: no control store, or it cannot be read.

```
orca gc
orca gc --older-than 7 --keep-last 3
orca gc --apply --group my-group
orca gc --apply --include-uncleaned --older-than 30
orca gc --json
```

## `orca doctor`

status's checks plus slower ones (agent CLIs on the service PATH, ~/.orca modes, stale sockets), with one fix line per failure (read-only)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.
- Exit codes: 0 every check ok (warnings allowed); 1 a check failed.

```
orca doctor
```

## `orca version`

the CLI's version (the orca-control skill's version: should equal it)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.

```
orca version
orca version --json
```

## `orca login --name <name> [--password-stdin]`

store a person token by typing the panel account's password here (members and isolated test panels; otherwise prefer orca auth login); used only with --as-person

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `--name <name>` (required): the panel account to log in as
- `--password-stdin`: an isolated test panel only: read the password as one line from stdin (refused for any path under the real ~/.orca)

```
orca login --name ana
printf '%s\n' "$PW" | orca login --name tester --password-stdin --control-state-dir /tmp/test-panel/state
orca usage set-cap --scope all --period week --tokens 500000 --as-person
```

## `orca logout`

revoke the stored person token and remove it

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).

```
orca logout
```

## `orca help [<topic>...]`

this list, or one domain's or one command's help (with --json: the same as data)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.
- `<topic>` (optional) (one or more): a domain, or a domain and an action

```
orca help
orca help group
orca help group start
orca help group show --json
```
